title: Man. Post. Cap. II: similitudes — cannot refuse; condition worsened
pass_a_gloss: As it is not in the power of him who is punished to admit the penalty, or not admit it, or even to shake it off, so we are affected by that corruption from another, and it is not situated in us not to admit it, or to shake it off. As the penalty of him on whom it is inflicted changes the condition into a worse, so Adam stained by this corruption became worse, more ignoble, fouler, more miserable, than he otherwise would have been.
pass_b_english: A punished person cannot choose to take the penalty, refuse it, or cast it off. We are hit by this corruption from another in the same way: refusing or casting it off is not in our power. A penalty also worsens the state of the one it strikes. Stained by this corruption, Adam became worse—more ignoble, fouler, more wretched—than he would have been without it.
source_text: Ut non est in ejus qui punitur potestate poenam admittere, vel non admittere aut etiam excutere, sic ab alio corruptione ista afficimur, nec in nobis situm est eam non admittere, aut excutere. Ut poena ejus cui infligitur conditionem mutat in deteriorem, sic hac corruptione inquinatus Adamus deterior, ignobilior, foedior, miserior, quam alioqui fuisset, evasit.

lemmas.gloss: changes the condition for the worse

notes: Cap. II Posterior quaestio de poena densify section 203 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 185 tip–186 tip).
